traceability.notes:
The story 025.0-DEV-CATCH-ANNOTATION-POSITION is only partially implemented. Core functional requirements are satisfied: - CatchClause annotations are detected both before the catch keyword and as first comments inside the catch block (REQ-DUAL-POSITION-DETECTION, REQ-FALLBACK-LOGIC), with correct priority given to before-catch annotations (REQ-POSITION-PRIORITY). - Auto-fix behavior for CatchClause inserts annotations inside the catch body at the first statement (REQ-PRETTIER-AUTOFIX), which aligns with how Prettier preserves comments, and this is exercised by dedicated unit tests. - The require-branch-annotation rule still handles CatchClause via DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES, and the entire rule test suite passes, indicating no regressions to other branch types.
However, not all acceptance criteria and Definition of Done items are met: - There is no explicit end-to-end Prettier integration test that formats code and then runs the rule, despite the story’s acceptance criteria and DoD calling this out as an outstanding item; the story itself marks the Prettier compatibility criterion and the Prettier integration test as unchecked. - The rule documentation (docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md) has not been updated to describe the dual valid positions for CatchClause annotations or to mention Prettier/formatter compatibility, and the story DoD explicitly marks documentation updates as pending.
Because these documentation and explicit integration-test criteria are part of the story’s acceptance criteria/DoD and remain unimplemented, the story cannot be considered fully complete, so the assessment status is FAILED.
